summary.headline: Julian’s Astrological Excerpts
summary.text: Discussion of excerpts attributed to Julian, the astrologer of the year 379: doctrine on the effects of thirty fixed stars, degrees causing injury, and Christian alterations to pagan divine names, apparitions, sacrifices, and demon conjurations. The discussion compares Parisian, Venetian, and Angelicus codices, questions the attribution of lunar configuration chapters, notes Arabic star names and repeated citations of Vettius Valens, and introduces brief notes on degrees injurious to the eyes.
